Britain's Best Biker Pubs: Our Top Picks

The British pub is one of the great institutions, and for motorcycle tourers, a good pub is the perfect end to a day's riding. The best biker pubs combine good food, real ales, secure parking, and a genuine welcome for riders. Here are our favourites from every corner of Britain.

Scotland

The Clachaig Inn, Glen Coe — Possibly the most dramatically situated pub in Britain. Nestled at the foot of the Three Sisters, with a beer garden that faces the mountains. Real ales, proper food, and accommodation. Every Highland tour should include a night here.

The Applecross Inn — The reward at the bottom of the Bealach na Bà. Famous for hand-dived scallops and local prawns. Book well ahead in summer — it's an open secret. The beer garden overlooks Applecross Bay with views to Skye.

The Torridon Inn, Annat — Informal pub attached to the Torridon hotel. Superb food using local Highland ingredients, with Liathach looming outside the window. Bike-friendly and welcoming.

Northern England

The Tan Hill Inn — Britain's highest pub at 528 metres, reachable by the most exhilarating road in the Yorkshire Dales. Remote, atmospheric, and genuinely unique. They occasionally get snowed in for days. Real ales and honest food.

The Kirkstone Pass Inn, Lake District — One of England's highest pubs, at the summit of the Kirkstone Pass. Log fires, traditional food, and a sense of earned refreshment after climbing the Struggle from Ambleside.

Wales

The Plas yn Dre, Bala — Excellent gastropub on the shores of Bala Lake, gateway to Bwlch y Groes and the Evo Triangle roads. Local Welsh lamb and fresh lake fish.

The Sloop Inn, Porthgain — Quirky harbour pub on the Pembrokeshire coast. Outstanding seafood in a converted harbour building. The approach road through tiny villages adds to the experience.

A good biker pub understands that riders arrive hungry, thirsty, and sometimes wet. The best ones have a boot room for drying gear and don't flinch when you walk in wearing leathers.

Southern and Central England

  • The Wheatsheaf, Northleach — Cotswolds gastropub with rooms, excellent food and wine
  • The Bull, Fairford — Classic Cotswolds coaching inn with bike parking in the courtyard
  • The Bankes Arms, Studland — Dorset coast pub with views across Poole Harbour, superb seafood
  • The Pilchard Inn, Burgh Island — Devon's most atmospheric pub, accessible only at low tide
  • The Old Dungeon Ghyll, Langdale — Lake District legend, beloved by walkers and bikers alike

What to Look For

The best biker pubs offer: visible or secure parking (essential for peace of mind), drying facilities for wet gear, food served at flexible hours (not just 12-2 and 6-9), real ales from local breweries, and accommodation for overnight stops. Many of the best pubs are in remote locations, so check opening hours and food service times before making a long detour. keyTakeaways: The Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe and the Applecross Inn are Scotland's standout biker pubs, both offering food, real ales and accommodation in dramatic settings.
England's high-altitude pubs like the Tan Hill Inn (528m, Britain's highest) and the Kirkstone Pass Inn reward the climb with log fires and honest food.
The best biker pubs offer visible or secure parking, drying facilities for wet gear and flexible food service beyond the standard 12-2 and 6-9 windows.
Remote favourites such as the Applecross Inn and the Sloop Inn at Porthgain require advance booking in summer, so plan long detours carefully.

faq.q: What makes a pub genuinely biker-friendly?
faq.a: The best biker pubs understand that riders arrive hungry, thirsty and sometimes wet. They offer visible or secure parking for peace of mind, a boot room or drying space for soaked gear, real ales from local breweries and food served at flexible hours rather than only the standard lunch and evening windows.

faq.q: Which is Britain's highest biker pub?
faq.a: The Tan Hill Inn in the Yorkshire Dales is Britain's highest pub at 528 metres, reached by one of the most exhilarating roads in the Dales. It is remote and atmospheric, occasionally gets snowed in for days, and serves real ales and honest food. The Kirkstone Pass Inn in the Lake District is another of England's highest.

faq.q: Do I need to book ahead at remote biker pubs?
faq.a: Yes, particularly in summer. The Applecross Inn, famous for hand-dived scallops and local prawns, is an open secret and fills quickly, so book well ahead. Many of the best pubs sit in remote locations, so always check opening hours and food service times before committing to a long detour.

faq.q: Can I stay overnight at these pubs?
faq.a: Many of the best biker pubs offer accommodation, which makes them ideal for touring. The Clachaig Inn in Glen Coe, the Applecross Inn and the Torridon Inn all have rooms, letting you enjoy a few local ales and a proper meal without worrying about riding on afterwards.

faq.q: Where are the best biker pubs in Scotland?
faq.a: The Clachaig Inn, nestled at the foot of the Three Sisters in Glen Coe, is possibly the most dramatically situated pub in Britain, with a beer garden facing the mountains. The Applecross Inn at the bottom of the Bealach na Ba and the Torridon Inn at Annat are two more Highland favourites serving outstanding local produce.
